prompt.context: Our client, Bun on the Run, operates a fast food restaurant chain. The industry's average profit margin is 3 to 5%. However, our client currently is making only 1.5%.
prompt.question: How can you help them increase their margins to 3%?

clarifying_info.a: The fast food outlets are on toll roads and in airports. The airport outlets are franchises.

clarifying_info.q: Which part of the business is driving the low margins?
clarifying_info.a: Airports constitute most of their business, and the low profit margins are due to their airport business.
The industry is fairly mature and stagnant.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's market position?
clarifying_info.a: The client operates in 80% of airports and is present in all large airports; they service 90% of all airport passengers.
There is only one other competitor, who has the remaining 10% market share; their margins are on par with the industry.

clarifying_info.q: What does the menu look like?
clarifying_info.a: Standard fast food menu; competitor is no different.
Variable costs are 70% of revenue (COGS 35%, Labor 35%). Fixed costs are 30% (Airport fee 10%, Infrastructure 5%, Rent 15%).

Core ingredients (bread, meat, etc.) are 70% of COGS and are already optimized — costs cannot be cut further. Non-core ingredients (paper towels, ketchup, etc.) are 30% of COGS and are contracted through SYSCO at competitive rates.

Most employees are salaried and full-time, earning minimum wage of $6/hour. Benefits start after 6 months. Turnover is 200%. A new employee costs an additional $18/hour — this cost includes training (4 weeks) and background check.

framework: Revenue: check pricing power, volume, and mix given mature/saturated market
Costs: break into variable (COGS, Labor) and fixed (airport fee, infrastructure, rent)
Narrow to Labor given high variable cost; drill into turnover rate and its drivers
Identify root cause: 200% turnover means constant retraining cost of $18/hr on top of $6/hr wage
Solutions: reduce turnover to lower training costs and stabilize labor cost structure

questions.prompt: Walk through the cost structure and identify where the margin problem originates.
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment costs into variable (70%) and fixed (30%). COGS at 35% is already optimized. Labor at 35% with 200% turnover is the key lever. A strong candidate identifies that the $18/hr training cost added to $6/hr wage means a new employee effectively costs $24/hr — 4x the baseline wage — making high turnover extremely expensive.

math.setup: Training cost per new employee is $18/hr additional on top of $6/hr base wage. At 200% annual turnover, the average employee tenure is 6 months (1/2 year). Evaluate effective hourly cost per productive employee-hour.
steps: 200% turnover means workforce turns over twice per year; average employee stays ~6 months
Training period is 4 weeks (~1 month), so roughly 1/6 of average tenure is spent in expensive training mode
This training cost continuously erodes the labor margin
math.answer: High turnover (200%) means training costs ($18/hr) are continuously incurred, dramatically inflating effective labor costs above the 35% baseline.

questions.prompt: What recommendations would you make to reduce turnover and improve margins?
questions.guidance: Good answer: identify the need to reduce turnover and retain employees longer. Better answer: suggest making benefits available earlier (before 6-month mark) and paying above minimum wage to compete with nearby McDonalds. Superior answer: propose low-cost retention levers such as cross-training for job variety and satisfaction, while flagging that cross-training may reduce utilization efficiency as a trade-off.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific actions could Bun on the Run take to increase employee retention and reduce training costs?

categories.name: Compensation & Benefits
ideas: Raise wages above minimum wage ($6/hr) to compete with McDonalds
Offer benefits earlier than the 6-month threshold to reduce early attrition
Introduce performance bonuses tied to tenure milestones

categories.name: Job Satisfaction & Development
ideas: Implement cross-training across roles to increase variety and engagement
Create clear career advancement path within the chain

categories.name: Hiring & Onboarding
ideas: Target candidates less likely to be poached (e.g., older workers, students needing flexible hours)
Streamline background checks to reduce pre-work cost
Shorten or improve training program efficiency to reduce $18/hr training cost

categories.name: Work Environment
ideas: Improve scheduling flexibility to reduce voluntary departures
Foster team culture in individual airport locations
Survey departing employees to identify root causes of attrition

recommendation: The primary driver of below-industry margins is a 200% employee turnover rate that continuously triggers expensive training costs ($18/hr on top of $6/hr base wages)
Recommend a retention-focused labor strategy: accelerate benefits eligibility before the 6-month mark and selectively raise wages above minimum wage to reduce attrition
Additionally, introduce cross-training to improve job satisfaction with minimal incremental cost, while monitoring utilization impact
risks: Raising wages increases the labor cost baseline, partially offsetting turnover savings — must model breakeven retention rate
Cross-training may reduce per-role productivity/utilization in the short term
Competitor could respond with similar retention measures, limiting competitive advantage
next_steps: Model breakeven: calculate the wage increase needed to reduce turnover enough to offset higher base pay
Pilot early-benefits and cross-training programs in 2-3 airport locations and measure turnover and margin impact
Review SYSCO contract and airport fee structures for any renegotiation opportunities as secondary levers
